const WORD_CODE_POINT = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
const MARK_CODE_POINT = /\p{M}/u;
const HAN = /\p{Script=Han}/u;
const HIRAGANA = /\p{Script=Hiragana}/u;
const KATAKANA = /\p{Script=Katakana}/u;
const HANGUL = /\p{Script=Hangul}/u;
const APOSTROPHES = new Set(["\u0027", "\u2019"]);

/** True when the code point is counted as one word by itself. */
export function isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return HAN.test(codePoint) || HIRAGANA.test(codePoint) || KATAKANA.test(codePoint) || HANGUL.test(codePoint);
}

function isWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return WORD_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint) || MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint);
}

function isJoinableApostrophe(text: string, index: number, inRun: boolean): boolean {
	if (!inRun || !APOSTROPHES.has(text[index] ?? "")) return false;
	const next = text[index + 1];
	return next !== undefined && isWordCodePoint(next) && !isStandaloneWordCodePoint(next);
}

/**
 * Count words with a deterministic Unicode code-point algorithm.
 *
 * Definition:
 * - NFC normalization is applied only to the counting copy.
 * - Each Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or Hangul letter is one word. A Chinese
 *   paragraph therefore has one word per ideograph, never one word total.
 * - A maximal run of other Unicode letters/numbers/marks is one word.
 * - U+0027 and U+2019 join a run only when both sides are non-CJK word code points.
 * - Combining marks never start a word.
 * - Punctuation, symbols, emoji, and whitespace are not words. Hyphens split,
 *   decimal points split, and URLs split at punctuation.
 */
export function countWords(input: string): number {
	const text = input.normalize("NFC");
	let count = 0;
	let inRun = false;
	let previousWasStandalone = false;

	for (let index = 0; index < text.length; ) {
		const codePoint = String.fromCodePoint(text.codePointAt(index) ?? 0);
		const width = codePoint.length;
		if (isJoinableApostrophe(text, index, inRun)) {
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			count++;
			inRun = false;
			previousWasStandalone = true;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint)) {
			// Marks belong to the preceding code point and never create a token.
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			if (!inRun && !previousWasStandalone) count++;
			inRun = true;
			previousWasStandalone = false;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		inRun = false;
		previousWasStandalone = false;
		index += width;
	}

	return count;
}

export interface WordLimitResult {
	readonly ok: boolean;
	readonly words: number;
	readonly maxWords: number;
	readonly remaining: number;
}

/** Evaluate a word cap without mutating the supplied text. */
export function evaluateWordLimit(input: string, maxWords: number): WordLimitResult {
	if (!Number.isInteger(maxWords) || maxWords < 0) {
		throw new RsiError("INTERNAL", "maxWords must be a non-negative integer.");
	}
	const words = countWords(input);
	return {
		ok: words <= maxWords,
		words,
		maxWords,
		remaining: Math.max(0, maxWords - words),
	};
}

/** Throw when text exceeds a word cap. The caller must not write on this error. */
export function assertWordLimit(
	input: string,
	maxWords: number,
	code: "MEMORY_WORD_LIMIT" | "DOCUMENT_WORD_LIMIT",
	label: string,
): number {
	const result = evaluateWordLimit(input, maxWords);
	if (!result.ok) {
		throw new RsiError(code, `${label} exceeds ${maxWords} words (found ${result.words}).`, {
			details: { words: result.words, maxWords },
		});
	}
	return result.words;
}

export const DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE = "UTC";
export const CLOCK_FORMAT_PATTERN = /^\d{4}\/\d{2}\/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$/;

export interface Clock {
	now(): Date;
}

/** Wall-clock source for the Supervisor and for tests injected into the Worker. */
export class SystemClock implements Clock {
	now(): Date {
		return new Date();
	}
}

/** Validate an IANA time zone or "UTC"; throws CONFIG_INVALID otherwise. */
export function assertValidTimeZone(timeZone: string): string {
	if (timeZone.trim().length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", "timeZone must not be empty.");
	}
	try {
		new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone }).format(0);
	} catch (error) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", `Invalid IANA time zone: ${timeZone}`, { cause: error });
	}
	return timeZone;
}

export interface ZonedParts {
	readonly year: number;
	readonly month: number;
	readonly day: number;
	readonly hour: number;
	readonly minute: number;
	readonly second: number;
}

export interface WallClock extends ZonedParts {}

function formatterFor(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
	return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
		timeZone,
		calendar: "gregory",
		numberingSystem: "latn",
		hourCycle: "h23",
		year: "numeric",
		month: "2-digit",
		day: "2-digit",
		hour: "2-digit",
		minute: "2-digit",
		second: "2-digit",
	});
}

/** Read civil time fields in a specific zone. */
export function getZonedParts(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): ZonedParts {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const date = typeof instant === "number" ? new Date(instant) : instant;
	if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid Date value.");
	}
	const parts = formatterFor(timeZone).formatToParts(date);
	const values = new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));
	const read = (name: Intl.DateTimeFormatPartTypes): number => {
		const value = values.get(name);
		if (value === undefined) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", `Missing ${name} in time zone formatting.`);
		return Number(value);
	};
	return {
		year: read("year"),
		month: read("month"),
		day: read("day"),
		hour: read("hour") % 24,
		minute: read("minute"),
		second: read("second"),
	};
}

export function isLeapYear(year: number): boolean {
	return year % 4 === 0 && (year % 100 !== 0 || year % 400 === 0);
}

export function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
	switch (month) {
		case 2:
			return isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : 28;
		case 4:
		case 6:
		case 9:
		case 11:
			return 30;
		default:
			return 31;
	}
}

function assertCivilDate(parts: WallClock): void {
	if (
		!Number.isInteger(parts.year) ||
		parts.year < 1 ||
		parts.year > 9999 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.month) ||
		parts.month < 1 ||
		parts.month > 12 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.day) ||
		parts.day < 1 ||
		parts.day > daysInMonth(parts.year, parts.month) ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.hour) ||
		parts.hour < 0 ||
		parts.hour > 23 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.minute) ||
		parts.minute < 0 ||
		parts.minute > 59 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.second) ||
		parts.second < 0 ||
		parts.second > 59
	) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid civil date/time.");
	}
}

function utcMsFromCivil(parts: WallClock): number {
	const date = new Date(0);
	date.setUTCFullYear(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day);
	date.setUTCHours(parts.hour, parts.minute, parts.second, 0);
	return date.getTime();
}

function nextDay(parts: WallClock): WallClock {
	const date = new Date(utcMsFromCivil({ ...parts, hour: 0, minute: 0, second: 0 }));
	date.setUTCDate(date.getUTCDate() + 1);
	return {
		year: date.getUTCFullYear(),
		month: date.getUTCMonth() + 1,
		day: date.getUTCDate(),
		hour: 0,
		minute: 0,
		second: 0,
	};
}

/**
 * Parse the exact wall-clock syntax YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss.
 *
 * 24:00:00 is accepted only when minute and second are both zero, and is
 * normalized to 00:00:00 on the next civil day. 24:00:01 is invalid.
 */
export function parseWallClock(input: string): WallClock {
	const match = /^(\d{4})\/(\d{2})\/(\d{2}) (\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(input);
	if (!match) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Expected YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss.");
	}
	const [, yearText, monthText, dayText, hourText, minuteText, secondText] = match;
	const parts: WallClock = {
		year: Number(yearText),
		month: Number(monthText),
		day: Number(dayText),
		hour: Number(hourText),
		minute: Number(minuteText),
		second: Number(secondText),
	};
	if (parts.hour === 24) {
		if (parts.minute !== 0 || parts.second !== 0) {
			throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "24:00:00 is the only valid hour-24 spelling.");
		}
		const rolled = nextDay({ ...parts, hour: 0 });
		assertCivilDate(rolled);
		return rolled;
	}
	assertCivilDate(parts);
	return parts;
}

/** Format parsed civil fields as the canonical second-resolution timestamp. */
export function formatWallClock(parts: WallClock): string {
	assertCivilDate(parts);
	const pad = (value: number, width: number): string => String(value).padStart(width, "0");
	return `${pad(parts.year, 4)}/${pad(parts.month, 2)}/${pad(parts.day, 2)} ${pad(parts.hour, 2)}:${pad(parts.minute, 2)}:${pad(parts.second, 2)}`;
}

/** Normalize a wall-clock string, including the only legal 24:00:00 spelling. */
export function normalizeWallClock(input: string): string {
	return formatWallClock(parseWallClock(input));
}

/** Offset of a zone at an instant, in milliseconds east of UTC. */
export function getTimeZoneOffsetMs(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): number {
	const epochMs = typeof instant === "number" ? instant : instant.getTime();
	if (!Number.isFinite(epochMs)) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid instant.");
	const wholeSecond = Math.trunc(epochMs / 1_000) * 1_000;
	const parts = getZonedParts(wholeSecond, timeZone);
	return utcMsFromCivil(parts) - wholeSecond;
}

export interface ParsedZonedDateTime {
	readonly timeZone: string;
	readonly epochMs: number;
	readonly normalized: string;
	readonly ambiguous: boolean;
}

/**
 * Resolve a wall-clock string in a zone.
 *
 * A skipped local time (spring-forward gap) is an error. An ambiguous local
 * time (fall-back overlap) resolves to the earlier instant and reports
 * `ambiguous: true`; this policy is deterministic across hosts.
 */
export function parseZonedDateTime(input: string, timeZone: string): ParsedZonedDateTime {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const wallClock = parseWallClock(input);
	const targetMs = utcMsFromCivil(wallClock);
	const offsetCandidates = new Set<number>();
	const oneHour = 3_600_000;
	for (let deltaHours = -36; deltaHours <= 36; deltaHours++) {
		offsetCandidates.add(getTimeZoneOffsetMs(targetMs + deltaHours * oneHour, timeZone));
	}
	const matches: number[] = [];
	for (const offset of offsetCandidates) {
		const candidate = targetMs - offset;
		const candidateParts = getZonedParts(candidate, timeZone);
		if (
			candidateParts.year === wallClock.year &&
			candidateParts.month === wallClock.month &&
			candidateParts.day === wallClock.day &&
			candidateParts.hour === wallClock.hour &&
			candidateParts.minute === wallClock.minute &&
			candidateParts.second === wallClock.second

			matches.push(candidate);
		}

		timeZone,
		epochMs: matches[0] ?? targetMs,
		normalized: formatWallClock(wallClock),
		ambiguous: matches.length > 1,
	};

export const DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE = "UTC";

export interface Clock {
	now(): Date;
}

/** Wall-clock source for the Supervisor and for tests injected into the Worker. */
export class SystemClock implements Clock {
	now(): Date {
		return new Date();
	}
}

/** Validate an IANA time zone or "UTC"; throws CONFIG_INVALID otherwise. */
export function assertValidTimeZone(timeZone: string): string {
	if (timeZone.trim().length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", "timeZone must not be empty.");
	}
	try {
		new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone }).format(0);
	} catch (error) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", `Invalid IANA time zone: ${timeZone}`, { cause: error });
	}
	return timeZone;
}

export interface ZonedParts {
	readonly year: number;
	readonly month: number;
	readonly day: number;
	readonly hour: number;
	readonly minute: number;
	readonly second: number;
}

export interface WallClock extends ZonedParts {}

function formatterFor(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
	return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
		timeZone,
		calendar: "gregory",
		numberingSystem: "latn",
		hourCycle: "h23",
		year: "numeric",
		month: "2-digit",
		day: "2-digit",
		hour: "2-digit",
		minute: "2-digit",
		second: "2-digit",
	});
}

export function getZonedParts(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): ZonedParts {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const date = typeof instant === "number" ? new Date(instant) : instant;
	if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid Date value.");
	}
	const parts = formatterFor(timeZone).formatToParts(date);
	const values = new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));

		const value = values.get(name);
		if (value === undefined) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", `Missing ${name} in time zone formatting.`);
		return Number(value);
	};

		year: read("year"),
		month: read("month"),
		day: read("day"),
		hour: read("hour") % 24,
		minute: read("minute"),
		second: read("second"),
	};
}

export function isLeapYear(year: number): boolean {
	return year % 4 === 0 && (year % 100 !== 0 || year % 400 === 0);
}

export function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
	switch (month) {
		case 2:
			return isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : 28;
		case 4:
		case 6:
		case 9:
		case 11:
			return 30;
		default:
			return 31;
	}
}

function assertCivilDate(parts: WallClock): void {
	if (
		!Number.isInteger(parts.year) ||
		parts.year < 1 ||
		parts.year > 9999 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.month) ||
		parts.month < 1 ||
		parts.month > 12 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.day) ||
		parts.day < 1 ||
		parts.day > daysInMonth(parts.year, parts.month) ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.hour) ||
		parts.hour < 0 ||
		parts.hour > 23 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.minute) ||
		parts.minute < 0 ||
		parts.minute > 59 ||

		parts.second < 0 ||
		parts.second > 59

	const date = new Date(0);
	date.setUTCFullYear(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day);
	date.setUTCHours(parts.hour, parts.minute, parts.second, 0);
	return date.getTime();
}

	const date = new Date(utcMsFromCivil({ ...parts, hour: 0, minute: 0, second: 0 }));
	date.setUTCDate(date.getUTCDate() + 1);
	return {
		year: date.getUTCFullYear(),
		month: date.getUTCMonth() + 1,
		day: date.getUTCDate(),
		hour: 0,
		minute: 0,
		second: 0,

export function parseWallClock(input: string): WallClock {

const MARK_CODE_POINT = /\p{M}/u;
const HAN = /\p{Script=Han}/u;
const HIRAGANA = /\p{Script=Hiragana}/u;

const HANGUL = /\p{Script=Hangul}/u;

/** True when the code point is counted as one word by itself. */
export function isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return HAN.test(codePoint) || HIRAGANA.test(codePoint) || KATAKANA.test(codePoint) || HANGUL.test(codePoint);
}

function isWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return WORD_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint) || MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint);
}

function isJoinableApostrophe(text: string, index: number, inRun: boolean): boolean {
	if (!inRun || !APOSTROPHES.has(text[index] ?? "")) return false;
	const next = text[index + 1];
	return next !== undefined && isWordCodePoint(next) && !isStandaloneWordCodePoint(next);

/**
 * Count words with a deterministic Unicode code-point algorithm.
 *
 * Definition:
 * - NFC normalization is applied only to the counting copy.
 * - Each Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or Hangul letter is one word. A Chinese
 *   paragraph therefore has one word per ideograph, never one word total.
 * - A maximal run of other Unicode letters/numbers/marks is one word.
 * - U+0027 and U+2019 join a run only when both sides are non-CJK word code points.
 * - Combining marks never start a word.
 * - Punctuation, symbols, emoji, and whitespace are not words. Hyphens split,
 *   decimal points split, and URLs split at punctuation.
 */
export function countWords(input: string): number {
	const text = input.normalize("NFC");
	let count = 0;
	let inRun = false;
	let previousWasStandalone = false;

	for (let index = 0; index < text.length; ) {
		const codePoint = String.fromCodePoint(text.codePointAt(index) ?? 0);
		const width = codePoint.length;
		if (isJoinableApostrophe(text, index, inRun)) {
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			count++;
			inRun = false;
			previousWasStandalone = true;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint)) {
			// Marks belong to the preceding code point and never create a token.
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			if (!inRun && !previousWasStandalone) count++;
			inRun = true;
			previousWasStandalone = false;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		inRun = false;
		previousWasStandalone = false;
		index += width;
	}

	return count;

import { RsiError } from "./errors.ts";

const WORD_CODE_POINT = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
const MARK_CODE_POINT = /\p{M}/u;
const HAN = /\p{Script=Han}/u;
const HIRAGANA = /\p{Script=Hiragana}/u;
const KATAKANA = /\p{Script=Katakana}/u;
const HANGUL = /\p{Script=Hangul}/u;
const APOSTROPHES = new Set(["\u0027", "\u2019"]);

/** True when the code point is counted as one word by itself. */
export function isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return HAN.test(codePoint) || HIRAGANA.test(codePoint) || KATAKANA.test(codePoint) || HANGUL.test(codePoint);
}

function isWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return WORD_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint) || MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint);
}

function isJoinableApostrophe(text: string, index: number, inRun: boolean): boolean {
	if (!inRun || !APOSTROPHES.has(text[index] ?? "")) return false;
	const next = text[index + 1];
	return next !== undefined && isWordCodePoint(next) && !isStandaloneWordCodePoint(next);
}

/**
 * Count words with a deterministic Unicode code-point algorithm.
 *
 * Definition:
 * - NFC normalization is applied only to the counting copy.
 * - Each Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or Hangul letter is one word. A Chinese
 *   paragraph therefore has one word per ideograph, never one word total.
 * - A maximal run of other Unicode letters/numbers/marks is one word.
 * - U+0027 and U+2019 join a run only when both sides are non-CJK word code points.
 * - Combining marks never start a word.
 * - Punctuation, symbols, emoji, and whitespace are not words. Hyphens split,
 *   decimal points split, and URLs split at punctuation.
 */
export function countWords(input: string): number {
	const text = input.normalize("NFC");
	let count = 0;
	let inRun = false;
	let previousWasStandalone = false;

	for (let index = 0; index < text.length; ) {
		const codePoint = String.fromCodePoint(text.codePointAt(index) ?? 0);
		const width = codePoint.length;
		if (isJoinableApostrophe(text, index, inRun)) {
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			count++;
			inRun = false;
			previousWasStandalone = true;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint)) {
			// Marks belong to the preceding code point and never create a token.
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			if (!inRun && !previousWasStandalone) count++;
			inRun = true;
			previousWasStandalone = false;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		inRun = false;
		previousWasStandalone = false;
		index += width;
	}

	return count;
}

export interface WordLimitResult {
	readonly ok: boolean;
	readonly words: number;
	readonly maxWords: number;
	readonly remaining: number;
}

export function evaluateWordLimit(input: string, maxWords: number): WordLimitResult {

		throw new RsiError("INTERNAL", "maxWords must be a non-negative integer.");

	const words = countWords(input);
	return {
		ok: words <= maxWords,
		words,
		maxWords,
		remaining: Math.max(0, maxWords - words),
	};
}

/** Throw when text exceeds a word cap. The caller must not write on this error. */
export function assertWordLimit(
	input: string,
	maxWords: number,
	code: "MEMORY_WORD_LIMIT" | "DOCUMENT_WORD_LIMIT",
	label: string,
): number {

import { RsiError } from "./errors.ts";

export const DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE = "UTC";
export const CLOCK_FORMAT_PATTERN = /^\d{4}\/\d{2}\/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$/;

export interface Clock {
	now(): Date;
}

/** Wall-clock source for the Supervisor and for tests injected into the Worker. */
export class SystemClock implements Clock {
	now(): Date {
		return new Date();
	}
}

/** Validate an IANA time zone or "UTC"; throws CONFIG_INVALID otherwise. */
export function assertValidTimeZone(timeZone: string): string {
	if (timeZone.trim().length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", "timeZone must not be empty.");
	}
	try {
		new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone }).format(0);
	} catch (error) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", `Invalid IANA time zone: ${timeZone}`, { cause: error });
	}
	return timeZone;
}

export interface ZonedParts {
	readonly year: number;
	readonly month: number;
	readonly day: number;
	readonly hour: number;
	readonly minute: number;
	readonly second: number;
}

export interface WallClock extends ZonedParts {}

function formatterFor(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
	return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
		timeZone,
		calendar: "gregory",
		numberingSystem: "latn",
		hourCycle: "h23",
		year: "numeric",
		month: "2-digit",
		day: "2-digit",
		hour: "2-digit",
		minute: "2-digit",
		second: "2-digit",
	});
}

/** Read civil time fields in a specific zone. */
export function getZonedParts(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): ZonedParts {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const date = typeof instant === "number" ? new Date(instant) : instant;
	if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid Date value.");
	}
	const parts = formatterFor(timeZone).formatToParts(date);
	const values = new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));
	const read = (name: Intl.DateTimeFormatPartTypes): number => {
		const value = values.get(name);
		if (value === undefined) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", `Missing ${name} in time zone formatting.`);
		return Number(value);
	};
	return {
		year: read("year"),
		month: read("month"),
		day: read("day"),
		hour: read("hour") % 24,
		minute: read("minute"),
		second: read("second"),
	};
}

export function isLeapYear(year: number): boolean {
	return year % 4 === 0 && (year % 100 !== 0 || year % 400 === 0);
}

export function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
	switch (month) {
		case 2:
			return isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : 28;
		case 4:
		case 6:
		case 9:

			return 30;
		default:
			return 31;
	}

		!Number.isInteger(parts.year) ||

		parts.year > 9999 ||

		parts.month < 1 ||

		!Number.isInteger(parts.day) ||

		parts.hour < 0 ||
		parts.hour > 23 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.minute) ||
		parts.minute < 0 ||
		parts.minute > 59 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.second) ||
		parts.second < 0 ||

	const date = new Date(0);

	const date = new Date(utcMsFromCivil({ ...parts, hour: 0, minute: 0, second: 0 }));

		year: date.getUTCFullYear(),
		month: date.getUTCMonth() + 1,
		day: date.getUTCDate(),
		hour: 0,
		minute: 0,
		second: 0,

export function parseWallClock(input: string): WallClock {

		month: Number(monthText),

		hour: Number(hourText),

import type { ImageContent, SystemMessage, TextContent, ThinkingContent, ToolCall } from "../types.ts";

type Content = TextContent | ImageContent | ThinkingContent | ToolCall;

/** Extract and join text from message content. */
export function contentText(content: string | readonly Content[], separator = "\n"): string {
	if (typeof content === "string") return content;
	return content
		.filter((block) => block.type === "text")
		.map((block) => block.text)
		.join(separator);
}

/** Render a system message as a complete prompt: its content followed by its sections. */
export function getSystemMessageText(message: SystemMessage): string {
	const parts = [contentText(message.content)];
	for (const text of Object.values(message.sections ?? {})) {
		if (text !== null) parts.push(text);
	}
	return parts.filter((part) => part.length > 0).join("\n\n");
}

/**
 * Render a later system message for APIs that accept system messages mid-conversation.
 * Section changes are framed by name so the model can relate them to the leading prompt.
 * This framing is request-time only and may change between versions.
 */
export function renderSystemMessageUpdate(message: SystemMessage): string {
	const parts: string[] = [];
	const text = contentText(message.content);
	if (text.length > 0) parts.push(text);
	for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(message.sections ?? {})) {
		parts.push(
			value === null
				? `Removed system prompt section "${name}".`
				: `Updated system prompt section "${name}":\n\n${value}`,
		);
	}
	return parts.join("\n\n");
}

/**
 * `text.slice(start, end)` as a string of its own. V8 represents a slice of 13 or more characters as a view that keeps
 * all of `text` alive, so a short excerpt kept from a large text (a 500-character error message cut from a megabyte
 * response body) would keep the whole text alive as long as the excerpt lives. Appending a character and slicing it off
 * again makes V8 copy just the slice.
 */
export function ownedSlice(text: string, start: number, end = text.length): string {
	return `${text.slice(start, end)} `.slice(0, -1);
}

/**
 * Declare tool loadout changes to the model.
 *
 * `context.tools` is what the runtime can execute; the transcript's system messages declare
 * what the model may call. Before each request the difference becomes `toolsAdded` and
 * `toolsRemoved` on a system message. When a pending system message exists, its tool fields
 * are treated as intent and replaced with the delta between the committed transcript and
 * the executable set, so replay always yields exactly `context.tools`. Otherwise a new
 * system message is inserted before the first non-system pending message.
 */
function declareToolChanges(context: AgentContext, pendingMessages: AgentMessage[]): AgentMessage[] {
	let systemIndex = -1;
	for (let i = pendingMessages.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
		if (pendingMessages[i].role === "system") {
			systemIndex = i;
			break;
		}
	}
	const pending = pendingMessages[systemIndex] as SystemMessage | undefined;
	const baseline = pending
		? pendingMessages.map((message, index) =>
				index === systemIndex ? withToolChanges(pending, NO_CHANGES) : message,
			)
		: pendingMessages;
	const changes = getToolStateChanges(
		getCurrentTools([...context.messages, ...baseline]),
		(context.tools ?? []).map(toToolDeclaration),
	);
	const unchanged = changes.toolsAdded.length === 0 && changes.toolsRemoved.length === 0;

	if (pending) {
		// Keep the caller's message object when it already declares no tool changes.
		if (unchanged && !pending.toolsAdded?.length && !pending.toolsRemoved?.length) return pendingMessages;
		return baseline.map((message, index) => (index === systemIndex ? withToolChanges(pending, changes) : message));
	}
	if (unchanged) return pendingMessages;
	const update = withToolChanges({ role: "system", content: "", timestamp: Date.now() }, changes);
	const insertIndex = pendingMessages.findIndex((message) => message.role !== "system");
	const index = insertIndex === -1 ? pendingMessages.length : insertIndex;
	return [...pendingMessages.slice(0, index), update, ...pendingMessages.slice(index)];
}

const NO_CHANGES: ToolStateChanges = { toolsAdded: [], toolsRemoved: [] };

/** Copy a system message with its tool fields replaced by `changes`; empty lists omit the field. */
function withToolChanges(message: SystemMessage, { toolsAdded, toolsRemoved }: ToolStateChanges): SystemMessage {
	const { toolsAdded: _added, toolsRemoved: _removed, ...rest } = message;
	return {
		...rest,
		...(toolsAdded.length > 0 ? { toolsAdded } : {}),
		...(toolsRemoved.length > 0 ? { toolsRemoved } : {}),
	};
}

/**

 * This is where AgentMessage[] gets transformed to Message[] for the LLM.

async function streamAssistantResponse(

	config: AgentLoopConfig,
	signal: AbortSignal | undefined,
	emit: AgentEventSink,
	streamFunction: StreamFn,
): Promise<AssistantMessage> {

	let messages = context.messages;
	if (config.transformContext) {
		messages = await config.transformContext(messages, signal);

	// Convert to LLM-compatible messages (AgentMessage[] → Message[])
	const llmMessages = await config.convertToLlm(messages);

	const llmContext = normalizeContext({ messages: llmMessages });

		(config.getApiKey ? await config.getApiKey(config.model.provider) : undefined) || config.apiKey;

		...config,
		apiKey: resolvedApiKey,
		identity: mergeClientIdentity(DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY, config.identity),

	operations?: WriteOperations;
}

export function createWriteToolDefinition(

	options?: WriteToolOptions,
): ToolDefinition<typeof writeSchema, undefined> {
	const ops = options?.operations ?? defaultWriteOperations;
	return {
		name: "write",
		label: "write",
		description:
			"Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.",
		promptSnippet: writeToolSystemPromptContribution.snippet,
		promptGuidelines: [...writeToolSystemPromptContribution.guidelines],
		parameters: writeSchema,
		constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" },
		async execute(

				// Checking signal.aborted after each await observes the same aborts while

				const throwIfAborted = (): void => {
					if (signal?.aborted) throw new Error("Operation aborted");
				};

				await ops.writeFile(absolutePath, content);
				throwIfAborted();

				return {
					content: [{ type: "text", text: `Successfully wrote to ${path}` }],
					details: undefined,
				};
			});
		},
		...writeRenderers,
	};
}

export function createWriteTool(cwd: string, options?: WriteToolOptions): AgentTool<typeof writeSchema> {
	return wrapToolDefinition(createWriteToolDefinition(cwd, options));

/**
 * Replay every system message into one leading system message holding the current
 * prompt and tools. Later `content` is appended to the base prompt, `sections` are
 * patched by name, and tools are resolved with {@link getCurrentTools}.
 */
export function getCurrentSystemMessage(messages: TranscriptMessages): SystemMessage | undefined {
	const content: string[] = [];
	const sections = new Map<string, string>();
	let timestamp: number | undefined;
	for (const message of messages) {
		if (!isSystemMessage(message)) continue;
		timestamp ??= message.timestamp;
		const text = contentText(message.content);
		if (text.length > 0) content.push(text);
		for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(message.sections ?? {})) {
			if (value === null) sections.delete(name);
			else sections.set(name, value);
		}
	}
	const tools = getCurrentTools(messages);
	if (timestamp === undefined && tools.length === 0) return undefined;
	return {
		role: "system",
		content: content.join("\n\n"),
		...(sections.size > 0 ? { sections: Object.fromEntries(sections) } : {}),
		...(tools.length > 0 ? { toolsAdded: tools } : {}),
		timestamp: timestamp ?? 0,
	};
}

/** Render the current system prompt text after replaying every system message. */
export function getCurrentSystemPrompt(messages: TranscriptMessages): string {
	const message = getCurrentSystemMessage(messages);
	return message ? getSystemMessageText(message) : "";
}

/**
 * Rebuild the transcript for APIs without mid-conversation system messages: the replayed
 * system message leads, and every later system message is dropped.
 */
export function collapseSystemMessages(context: TranscriptContext): TranscriptContext {
	const head = getCurrentSystemMessage(context.messages);
	const messages = context.messages.filter((message) => message.role !== "system");
	return { messages: head ? [head, ...messages] : messages } as TranscriptContext;
}

/** Keep later system messages in place when the model accepts them; otherwise collapse them. */
export function resolveTranscript(
	context: TranscriptContext,
	supportsMidConvoSystemMessages: boolean | undefined,
): TranscriptContext {
	return supportsMidConvoSystemMessages ? context : collapseSystemMessages(context);
}

export function toToolDeclaration(tool: Tool): Tool {
	return {
		name: tool.name,
		description: tool.description,
		parameters: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(tool.parameters)) as Tool["parameters"],
		...(tool.constrainedSampling === undefined ? {} : { constrainedSampling: tool.constrainedSampling }),
	};
}

export function createEditToolDefinition(
	cwd: string,
	options?: EditToolOptions,
): ToolDefinition<typeof editSchema, EditToolDetails | undefined, EditRenderState> {
	const ops = options?.operations ?? defaultEditOperations;
	return {
		name: "edit",
		label: "edit",
		description:
			"Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. 		promptGuidelines: [...editToolSystemPromptContribution.guidelines],
		parameters: editSchema,
		constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" },
		renderShell: "self",
		prepareArguments: prepareEditArguments,
		async execute(_toolCallId, input: EditToolInput, signal?: AbortSignal, _onUpdate?, ctx?: ExtensionContext) {
			const { path, edits } = validateEditInput(input);
			const absolutePath = resolveToCwd(path, ctx?.cwd || cwd);

			return withFileMutationQueue(absolutePath, async () => {
				// Do not reject from an abort event listener here: that would release the
				// mutation queue while an in-flight filesystem operation may still finish.
				// Checking signal.aborted after each await observes the same aborts while
				// keeping the queue locked until the current operation has settled.
				const throwIfAborted = (): void => {
					if (signal?.aborted) throw new Error("Operation aborted");
				};

				throwIfAborted();

				// Check if file exists.
				try {
					await ops.access(absolutePath);
				} catch (error: unknown) {
					throwIfAborted();
					const errorMessage =

				}
				throwIfAborted();

				const rawContent = buffer.toString("utf-8");
				throwIfAborted();

				const originalEnding = detectLineEnding(content);
				const normalizedContent = normalizeToLF(content);

				const finalContent = bom + restoreLineEndings(newContent, originalEnding);
				await ops.writeFile(absolutePath, finalContent);

			});
		},

import type { ExtensionAPI } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
import type { Api, Model } from "@earendil-works/pi-ai";
import {
  hasExposedCandidate,
  hasUrlCandidate,
  resolveResolutionContext,
} from "../lib/candidates.ts";
import { buildWebSearchSchema, buildWebSearchToolDescription, WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME } from "../lib/schema.ts";
import { runWebSearch } from "../lib/search.ts";

export { WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME } from "../lib/schema.ts";

export function createWebSearchToolManager(
  pi: Pick<ExtensionAPI, "registerTool" | "getActiveTools" | "setActiveTools">,
) {
  let lastSignature: string | undefined;
  let preferredActive = true;
  let lastAppliedPresence: boolean | undefined;

  const register = (allowUrls: boolean, exposed = false): void => {
    pi.registerTool({
      name: WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME,
      label: "Web Search",
      description: buildWebSearchToolDescription({ allowUrls }),
      parameters: buildWebSearchSchema({ allowUrls }),
      exposure: "direct",
      defaultActive: false,
      annotations: { readOnlyHint: true, openWorldHint: true },
      execute: async (_toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) =>
        runWebSearch(params, ctx, signal, onUpdate),
    });
    lastSignature = `${exposed}|${allowUrls}`;
  };

  const sync = (
    ctx: Parameters<typeof resolveResolutionContext>[0],
    model?: Model<Api>,
  ): { expose: boolean; allowUrls: boolean } => {
    const resolution = resolveResolutionContext(ctx, model);
    const expose = hasExposedCandidate(resolution);
    const allowUrls = expose && hasUrlCandidate(resolution);
    const signature = `${expose}|${allowUrls}`;

    if (signature !== lastSignature) {
      // pi replaces a same-name definition, so this updates the schema
      // without ever registering a second tool.
      register(allowUrls, expose);
    }

    const current = pi.getActiveTools();
    const currentPresence = current.includes(WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME);

    if (lastAppliedPresence === undefined) {
      // Establish the baseline without interpreting the initial state as a
      // user preference change.
      lastAppliedPresence = currentPresence;
    } else if (currentPresence !== lastAppliedPresence) {
      // The user changed the active set outside sync. Remember that choice.
      preferredActive = currentPresence;
    }

    const desiredPresence = expose && preferredActive;
    if (desiredPresence !== currentPresence) {
      const next = current.filter((name) => name !== WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME);
      if (desiredPresence) next.push(WEB_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME);
      pi.setActiveTools(next);
    }

    lastAppliedPresence = desiredPresence;
    return { expose, allowUrls };
  };

  return { register, sync };
}

export default function piBetterWebSearch(pi: ExtensionAPI): void {
  const manager = createWebSearchToolManager(pi);
  manager.register(false);

  pi.on("session_start", (_event, ctx) => {
    manager.sync(ctx);
  });
  pi.on("session_tree", (_event, ctx) => {
    manager.sync(ctx);
  });
  pi.on("model_select", (event, ctx) => {
    manager.sync(ctx, event.model);
  });
  pi.on("before_agent_start", (_event, ctx) => {
    manager.sync(ctx);
  });
}

function getAliases(): Record<string, string> {
	if (_aliases) return _aliases;

	const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
	const packageIndex = path.resolve(__dirname, "../..", "index.js");

	const typeboxEntry = require.resolve("typebox");
	const typeboxCompileEntry = require.resolve("typebox/compile");
	const typeboxValueEntry = require.resolve("typebox/value");

	const packagesRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../../../");
	const resolveWorkspaceOrImport = (workspaceRelativePath: string, specifier: string): string => {
		const workspacePath = path.join(packagesRoot, workspaceRelativePath);
		if (fs.existsSync(workspacePath)) {
			return workspacePath;
		}
		return fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve(specifier));
	};

	const piCodingAgentEntry = packageIndex;
	const piAgentCoreEntry = resolveWorkspaceOrImport("agent/dist/index.js", "@earendil-works/pi-agent-core");
	const piTuiEntry = resolveWorkspaceOrImport("tui/dist/index.js", "@earendil-works/pi-tui");
	// Extensions resolve the pi-ai root to the compat entrypoint (a strict
	// superset of the core entrypoint): existing extensions using the old
	// global API keep working at runtime until compat is removed.
	const piAiCompatEntry = resolveWorkspaceOrImport("ai/dist/compat.js", "@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat");
	const piAiModelsEntry = resolveWorkspaceOrImport("ai/dist/models.js", "@earendil-works/pi-ai/models");
	const piAiOauthEntry = resolveWorkspaceOrImport("ai/dist/oauth.js", "@earendil-works/pi-ai/oauth");
	const piAiProvidersEntry = resolveWorkspaceOrImport(
		"ai/dist/providers/all.js",
		"@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/all",
	);

	_aliases = {
		"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": piCodingAgentEntry,
		"@earendil-works/pi-agent-core": piAgentCoreEntry,
		"@earendil-works/pi-tui": piTuiEntry,
		"@earendil-works/pi-ai/providers/all": piAiProvidersEntry,

		"@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent": piCodingAgentEntry,
		"@mariozechner/pi-agent-core": piAgentCoreEntry,
		"@mariozechner/pi-tui": piTuiEntry,

	return _aliases;
}

let extensionCacheCwd: string | undefined;
let extensionCacheGeneration = 0;
const extensionCache = new Map<string, ExtensionFactory>();

interface ExtensionCacheToken {
	cwd: string;
	generation: number;
}

export function clearExtensionCache(): void {
	extensionCache.clear();
	extensionCacheCwd = undefined;
	extensionCacheGeneration++;
}

function useExtensionCacheCwd(cwd: string): ExtensionCacheToken {
	const resolvedCwd = resolvePath(cwd);
	if (extensionCacheCwd !== undefined && extensionCacheCwd !== resolvedCwd) {
		clearExtensionCache();
	}
	extensionCacheCwd = resolvedCwd;
	return { cwd: resolvedCwd, generation: extensionCacheGeneration };
}

/**

export function createExtensionRuntime(): ExtensionRuntime {
	const notInitialized = () => {
		throw new Error("Extension runtime not initialized. Action methods cannot be called during extension loading.");
	};
	const state: { staleMessage?: string } = {};
	const eventBusUnsubscribers = new Set<() => void>();
	const assertActive = () => {
		if (state.staleMessage) {
			throw new Error(state.staleMessage);
		}
	};

	const runtime: ExtensionRuntime = {
		sendMessage: notInitialized,
		sendUserMessage: notInitialized,
		appendEntry: notInitialized,
		setSessionName: notInitialized,
		getSessionName: notInitialized,
		setLabel: notInitialized,
		getActiveTools: notInitialized,
		getAllTools: notInitialized,
		getSettings: notInitialized,

		refreshTools: () => {},
		getCommands: notInitialized,
		setModel: () => Promise.reject(new Error("Extension runtime not initialized")),
		getThinkingLevel: notInitialized,
		setThinkingLevel: notInitialized,
		flagValues: new Map(),
		pendingProviderRegistrations: [],
		pendingNativeProviderRegistrations: [],
		mcpServers: new McpServerRegistry(),
		pendingVirtualModelRegistrations: [],
		createContext: notInitialized,
		assertActive,
		invalidate: (message) => {
			if (state.staleMessage) return;
			state.staleMessage =
				message ??
				"This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload. Do not use a captured pi or command ctx after ctx.newSession(), ctx.fork(), ctx.switchSession(), or ctx.reload(). For newSession, fork, and switchSession, move post-replacement work into withSession and use the ctx passed to withSession. For reload, do not use the old ctx after await ctx.reload().";

function snapshotEventHandlers(extensions: Extension[], event: ExtensionEvent["type"]) {
	return extensions.map((ext) => ({ ext, handlers: ext.handlers.get(event)?.slice() ?? [] }));

function sameMessages(left: AgentMessage[], right: AgentMessage[]): boolean {
	return left.length === right.length && left.every((message, index) => message === right[index]);
}

/**
 * Re-attach the prompt and tool state after a `context` handler. Handlers only see the
 * conversation; the system messages belong to Pi. An unchanged conversation keeps every
 * system message in place, so models with mid-conversation support keep their cached
 * prefix. A changed one gets the replayed prompt sections and tool declarations as one
 * leading system message, so pruning, windowing, or slicing from a compaction summary
 * cannot drop them.
 */
function restoreSystemMessages(
	current: AgentMessage[],
	visible: AgentMessage[],
	returned: AgentMessage[],
): AgentMessage[] {
	if (sameMessages(returned, visible)) return current;
	const head = getCurrentSystemMessage(current);
	return head ? [head, ...returned] : returned;
}

export async function emitProjectTrustEvent(
	extensionsResult: LoadExtensionsResult,
	event: ProjectTrustEvent,
	ctx: ProjectTrustContext,
): Promise<{ result?: ProjectTrustEventResult; errors: ExtensionError[] }> {
	const errors: ExtensionError[] = [];
	for (const { ext, handlers } of snapshotEventHandlers(extensionsResult.extensions, "project_trust")) {
		// A single extension may register multiple handlers for the same event.
		// The first project_trust handler that returns yes/no wins; undecided falls through.
		for (const handler of handlers) {
			try {
				const handlerResult = (await handler(event, ctx)) as ProjectTrustEventResult;
				if (handlerResult.trusted === "undecided") {
					continue;
				}
				return { result: handlerResult, errors };
			} catch (error) {
				errors.push({
					extensionPath: ext.path,
					event: event.type,
					error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
					stack: error instanceof Error ? error.stack : undefined,
				});
			}
		}
	}
	return { errors };

		try {

/** Serializable error shape returned by IPC and written to control state. */
export interface RsiErrorPayload {
	readonly name: "RsiError";
	readonly code: RsiErrorCode;
	readonly message: string;
	readonly retryable: boolean;
	readonly details?: RsiJsonValue;
	readonly requestId?: string;
}

export interface RsiErrorOptions {
	readonly retryable?: boolean;
	readonly details?: RsiJsonValue;
	readonly requestId?: string;
	readonly cause?: unknown;
}

/** Error type that preserves its code and request id across process boundaries. */
export class RsiError extends Error {
	readonly code: RsiErrorCode;
	readonly retryable: boolean;
	readonly details: RsiJsonValue | undefined;
	readonly requestId: string | undefined;

	constructor(code: RsiErrorCode, message: string, options: RsiErrorOptions = {}) {
		super(message, options.cause === undefined ? undefined : { cause: options.cause });
		this.name = "RsiError";
		this.code = code;
		this.retryable = options.retryable ?? false;
		this.details = options.details;
		this.requestId = options.requestId;
	}

	toPayload(): RsiErrorPayload {
		return {
			name: "RsiError",
			code: this.code,
			message: this.message,
			retryable: this.retryable,
			...(this.details === undefined ? {} : { details: this.details }),
			...(this.requestId === undefined ? {} : { requestId: this.requestId }),
		};
	}
}

export function isRsiError(value: unknown): value is RsiError {
	return value instanceof RsiError;
}

export function hasErrorCode(value: unknown, code: RsiErrorCode): boolean {
	return isRsiError(value) && value.code === code;
}

/** Convert arbitrary thrown values to an RsiError while preserving known errors. */
export function asRsiError(
	error: unknown,
	fallbackCode: RsiErrorCode = "INTERNAL",
	fallbackMessage = "Unexpected runtime error",
): RsiError {
	if (isRsiError(error)) return error;
	const message = error instanceof Error && error.message.length > 0 ? error.message : fallbackMessage;
	return new RsiError(fallbackCode, message, { cause: error });
}

/** Build an error payload from an arbitrary thrown value. */
export function toRsiErrorPayload(
	error: unknown,
	fallbackCode: RsiErrorCode = "INTERNAL",
	requestId?: string,
): RsiErrorPayload {
	const rsiError = asRsiError(error, fallbackCode);
	const payload = rsiError.toPayload();
	return requestId === undefined ? payload : { ...payload, requestId };
}

/** Reconstruct an RsiError from a validated payload. */
export function rsiErrorFromPayload(payload: RsiErrorPayload): RsiError {
	return new RsiError(payload.code, payload.message, {
		retryable: payload.retryable,
		...(payload.details === undefined ? {} : { details: payload.details }),
		...(payload.requestId === undefined ? {} : { requestId: payload.requestId }),
	});
}

/** Validate an unknown value as an RsiErrorPayload. */
export function isRsiErrorPayload(value: unknown): value is RsiErrorPayload {
	if (typeof value !== "object" || value === null) return false;
	const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
	return (
		record.name === "RsiError" &&
		typeof record.code === "string" &&
		typeof record.message === "string" &&
		typeof record.retryable === "boolean"
	);
}

/** Pi command names that the agent must never be able to invoke. */

export type ForbiddenAgentControlCommand = (typeof FORBIDDEN_AGENT_CONTROL_COMMANDS)[number];

/** The agent loop only submits ordinary text, never Pi command/template expansion. */
export interface AgentPromptPolicy {
	readonly expandPromptTemplates: false;
	readonly rejectLeadingSlash: true;
}

export const AGENT_PROMPT_POLICY: AgentPromptPolicy = Object.freeze({
	expandPromptTemplates: false,
	rejectLeadingSlash: true,
});

/**
 * Reject a loop-originated prompt that could reach Pi's command dispatcher.
 *
 * This is a prompt-path guard, not an OS sandbox. Command calls from the trusted
 * Supervisor use the separate control channel and never pass through this guard.
 */
export function assertAgentPromptAllowed(text: string): void {
	if (text.trimStart().startsWith("/")) {
		throw new RsiError(
			"AGENT_COMMAND_FORBIDDEN",
			"Agent-originated prompts must not begin with '/' or invoke Pi command/control entry points.",
		);
	}
}

/** Validate the product-level MCP and Skill caps without changing Pi's native discovery rules. */
export function assertResourceCaps(input: { mcpServerCount: number; skillCount: number }): void {
	if (!Number.isInteger(input.mcpServerCount) || input.mcpServerCount < 0) {
		throw new RsiError("RESOURCE_CAP_EXCEEDED", "mcpServerCount must be a non-negative integer.");
	}
	if (!Number.isInteger(input.skillCount) || input.skillCount < 0) {
		throw new RsiError("RESOURCE_CAP_EXCEEDED", "skillCount must be a non-negative integer.");
	}
	if (input.mcpServerCount > MAX_MCP_SERVERS) {
		throw new RsiError("RESOURCE_CAP_EXCEEDED", `At most ${MAX_MCP_SERVERS} MCP servers may be configured.`);
	}
	if (input.skillCount > MAX_SKILLS) {
		throw new RsiError("RESOURCE_CAP_EXCEEDED", `At most ${MAX_SKILLS} Skills may be configured.`);
	}
}

const WORD_CODE_POINT = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
const MARK_CODE_POINT = /\p{M}/u;
const HAN = /\p{Script=Han}/u;
const HIRAGANA = /\p{Script=Hiragana}/u;
const KATAKANA = /\p{Script=Katakana}/u;
const HANGUL = /\p{Script=Hangul}/u;
const APOSTROPHES = new Set(["\u0027", "\u2019"]);

/** True when the code point is counted as one word by itself. */
export function isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return HAN.test(codePoint) || HIRAGANA.test(codePoint) || KATAKANA.test(codePoint) || HANGUL.test(codePoint);
}

function isWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return WORD_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint) || MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint);
}

function isJoinableApostrophe(text: string, index: number, inRun: boolean): boolean {
	if (!inRun || !APOSTROPHES.has(text[index] ?? "")) return false;
	const next = text[index + 1];
	return next !== undefined && isWordCodePoint(next) && !isStandaloneWordCodePoint(next);
}

/**
 * Count words with a deterministic Unicode code-point algorithm.
 *
 * Definition:
 * - NFC normalization is applied only to the counting copy.
 * - Each Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or Hangul letter is one word. A Chinese
 *   paragraph therefore has one word per ideograph, never one word total.
 * - A maximal run of other Unicode letters/numbers/marks is one word.
 * - U+0027 and U+2019 join a run only when both sides are non-CJK word code points.
 * - Combining marks never start a word.
 * - Punctuation, symbols, emoji, and whitespace are not words. Hyphens split,
 *   decimal points split, and URLs split at punctuation.
 */
export function countWords(input: string): number {
	const text = input.normalize("NFC");
	let count = 0;
	let inRun = false;
	let previousWasStandalone = false;

	for (let index = 0; index < text.length; ) {
		const codePoint = String.fromCodePoint(text.codePointAt(index) ?? 0);
		const width = codePoint.length;
		if (isJoinableApostrophe(text, index, inRun)) {
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			count++;
			inRun = false;
			previousWasStandalone = true;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint)) {
			// Marks belong to the preceding code point and never create a token.
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			if (!inRun && !previousWasStandalone) count++;
			inRun = true;
			previousWasStandalone = false;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		inRun = false;
		previousWasStandalone = false;
		index += width;
	}

	return count;
}

export interface WordLimitResult {
	readonly ok: boolean;
	readonly words: number;
	readonly maxWords: number;
	readonly remaining: number;
}

/** Evaluate a word cap without mutating the supplied text. */
export function evaluateWordLimit(input: string, maxWords: number): WordLimitResult {
	if (!Number.isInteger(maxWords) || maxWords < 0) {
		throw new RsiError("INTERNAL", "maxWords must be a non-negative integer.");
	}
	const words = countWords(input);
	return {
		ok: words <= maxWords,
		words,
		maxWords,
		remaining: Math.max(0, maxWords - words),
	};
}

/** Throw when text exceeds a word cap. The caller must not write on this error. */
export function assertWordLimit(
	input: string,
	maxWords: number,
	code: "MEMORY_WORD_LIMIT" | "DOCUMENT_WORD_LIMIT",

			details: { words: result.words, maxWords },
		});
	}
	return result.words;
}

export const DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE = "UTC";
export const CLOCK_FORMAT_PATTERN = /^\d{4}\/\d{2}\/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$/;

export interface Clock {
	now(): Date;
}

/** Wall-clock source for the Supervisor and for tests injected into the Worker. */
export class SystemClock implements Clock {
	now(): Date {
		return new Date();
	}
}

/** Validate an IANA time zone or "UTC"; throws CONFIG_INVALID otherwise. */
export function assertValidTimeZone(timeZone: string): string {
	if (timeZone.trim().length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", "timeZone must not be empty.");
	}
	try {
		new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone }).format(0);
	} catch (error) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", `Invalid IANA time zone: ${timeZone}`, { cause: error });
	}
	return timeZone;
}

export interface ZonedParts {
	readonly year: number;
	readonly month: number;
	readonly day: number;
	readonly hour: number;
	readonly minute: number;
	readonly second: number;
}

export interface WallClock extends ZonedParts {}

function formatterFor(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
	return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
		timeZone,
		calendar: "gregory",
		numberingSystem: "latn",
		hourCycle: "h23",
		year: "numeric",
		month: "2-digit",
		day: "2-digit",
		hour: "2-digit",
		minute: "2-digit",
		second: "2-digit",
	});
}

/** Read civil time fields in a specific zone. */
export function getZonedParts(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): ZonedParts {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const date = typeof instant === "number" ? new Date(instant) : instant;
	if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid Date value.");
	}
	const parts = formatterFor(timeZone).formatToParts(date);
	const values = new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));
	const read = (name: Intl.DateTimeFormatPartTypes): number => {
		const value = values.get(name);
		if (value === undefined) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", `Missing ${name} in time zone formatting.`);
		return Number(value);
	};
	return {
		year: read("year"),
		month: read("month"),
		day: read("day"),
		hour: read("hour") % 24,
		minute: read("minute"),
		second: read("second"),
	};
}

export function isLeapYear(year: number): boolean {
	return year % 4 === 0 && (year % 100 !== 0 || year % 400 === 0);
}

export function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
	switch (month) {
		case 2:
			return isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : 28;
		case 4:
		case 6:
		case 9:
		case 11:
			return 30;
		default:
			return 31;
	}
}

function assertCivilDate(parts: WallClock): void {
	if (
		!Number.isInteger(parts.year) ||
		parts.year < 1 ||
		parts.year > 9999 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.month) ||
		parts.month < 1 ||
		parts.month > 12 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.day) ||
		parts.day < 1 ||
		parts.day > daysInMonth(parts.year, parts.month) ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.hour) ||
		parts.hour < 0 ||
		parts.hour > 23 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.minute) ||
		parts.minute < 0 ||
		parts.minute > 59 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.second) ||
		parts.second < 0 ||
		parts.second > 59
	) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid civil date/time.");
	}
}

function utcMsFromCivil(parts: WallClock): number {
	const date = new Date(0);
	date.setUTCFullYear(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day);
	date.setUTCHours(parts.hour, parts.minute, parts.second, 0);
	return date.getTime();
}

function nextDay(parts: WallClock): WallClock {
	const date = new Date(utcMsFromCivil({ ...parts, hour: 0, minute: 0, second: 0 }));
	date.setUTCDate(date.getUTCDate() + 1);
	return {
		year: date.getUTCFullYear(),
		month: date.getUTCMonth() + 1,
		day: date.getUTCDate(),
		hour: 0,
		minute: 0,
		second: 0,
	};
}

/**
 * Parse the exact wall-clock syntax YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss.
 *
 * 24:00:00 is accepted only when minute and second are both zero, and is
 * normalized to 00:00:00 on the next civil day. 24:00:01 is invalid.
 */
export function parseWallClock(input: string): WallClock {
	const match = /^(\d{4})\/(\d{2})\/(\d{2}) (\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(input);
	if (!match) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Expected YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss.");
	}
	const [, yearText, monthText, dayText, hourText, minuteText, secondText] = match;
	const parts: WallClock = {
		year: Number(yearText),
		month: Number(monthText),
		day: Number(dayText),
		hour: Number(hourText),
		minute: Number(minuteText),
		second: Number(secondText),
	};
	if (parts.hour === 24) {
		if (parts.minute !== 0 || parts.second !== 0) {
			throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "24:00:00 is the only valid hour-24 spelling.");
		}
		const rolled = nextDay({ ...parts, hour: 0 });
		assertCivilDate(rolled);
		return rolled;
	}
	assertCivilDate(parts);
	return parts;
}

/** Format parsed civil fields as the canonical second-resolution timestamp. */
export function formatWallClock(parts: WallClock): string {
	assertCivilDate(parts);
	const pad = (value: number, width: number): string => String(value).padStart(width, "0");
	return `${pad(parts.year, 4)}/${pad(parts.month, 2)}/${pad(parts.day, 2)} ${pad(parts.hour, 2)}:${pad(parts.minute, 2)}:${pad(parts.second, 2)}`;
}

/** Normalize a wall-clock string, including the only legal 24:00:00 spelling. */
export function normalizeWallClock(input: string): string {
	return formatWallClock(parseWallClock(input));
}

/** Offset of a zone at an instant, in milliseconds east of UTC. */
export function getTimeZoneOffsetMs(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): number {
	const epochMs = typeof instant === "number" ? instant : instant.getTime();
	if (!Number.isFinite(epochMs)) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid instant.");
	const wholeSecond = Math.trunc(epochMs / 1_000) * 1_000;
	const parts = getZonedParts(wholeSecond, timeZone);
	return utcMsFromCivil(parts) - wholeSecond;
}

export interface ParsedZonedDateTime {
	readonly timeZone: string;
	readonly epochMs: number;
	readonly normalized: string;
	readonly ambiguous: boolean;
}

/**
 * Resolve a wall-clock string in a zone.
 *
 * A skipped local time (spring-forward gap) is an error. An ambiguous local
 * time (fall-back overlap) resolves to the earlier instant and reports
 * `ambiguous: true`; this policy is deterministic across hosts.
 */
export function parseZonedDateTime(input: string, timeZone: string): ParsedZonedDateTime {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const wallClock = parseWallClock(input);
	const targetMs = utcMsFromCivil(wallClock);
	const offsetCandidates = new Set<number>();
	const oneHour = 3_600_000;
	for (let deltaHours = -36; deltaHours <= 36; deltaHours++) {
		offsetCandidates.add(getTimeZoneOffsetMs(targetMs + deltaHours * oneHour, timeZone));
	}
	const matches: number[] = [];
	for (const offset of offsetCandidates) {
		const candidate = targetMs - offset;
		const candidateParts = getZonedParts(candidate, timeZone);
		if (
			candidateParts.year === wallClock.year &&
			candidateParts.month === wallClock.month &&
			candidateParts.day === wallClock.day &&
			candidateParts.hour === wallClock.hour &&
			candidateParts.minute === wallClock.minute &&
			candidateParts.second === wallClock.second
		) {
			matches.push(candidate);
		}
	}
	if (matches.length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_NONEXISTENT", `${input} does not exist in ${timeZone}.`, {
			details: { timeZone, input },
		});
	}
	matches.sort((left, right) => left - right);
	return {
		timeZone,
		epochMs: matches[0] ?? targetMs,
		normalized: formatWallClock(wallClock),
		ambiguous: matches.length > 1,
	};
}

/** Canonical tool/log timestamp: YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss in the configured zone. */
export function formatTimestamp(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): string {
	return formatWallClock(getZonedParts(instant, timeZone));
}

/** Logs include the zone because the tool suffix intentionally does not. */
export function formatLogTimestamp(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): string {
	return `${formatTimestamp(instant, timeZone)} ${timeZone}`;
}

export function currentTimeSuffix(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): string {
	return `(Current Time: ${formatTimestamp(instant, timeZone)})`;
}

/** The only suffix used for final tool-result decoration. */
export const CURRENT_TIME_SUFFIX_PATTERN = /\(Current Time: \d{4}\/\d{2}\/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\)/;

import { RsiError } from "./errors.ts";

const WORD_CODE_POINT = /[\p{L}\p{N}]/u;
const MARK_CODE_POINT = /\p{M}/u;
const HAN = /\p{Script=Han}/u;
const HIRAGANA = /\p{Script=Hiragana}/u;
const KATAKANA = /\p{Script=Katakana}/u;
const HANGUL = /\p{Script=Hangul}/u;
const APOSTROPHES = new Set(["\u0027", "\u2019"]);

/** True when the code point is counted as one word by itself. */
export function isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return HAN.test(codePoint) || HIRAGANA.test(codePoint) || KATAKANA.test(codePoint) || HANGUL.test(codePoint);
}

function isWordCodePoint(codePoint: string): boolean {
	return WORD_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint) || MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint);
}

function isJoinableApostrophe(text: string, index: number, inRun: boolean): boolean {
	if (!inRun || !APOSTROPHES.has(text[index] ?? "")) return false;
	const next = text[index + 1];
	return next !== undefined && isWordCodePoint(next) && !isStandaloneWordCodePoint(next);
}

/**
 * Count words with a deterministic Unicode code-point algorithm.
 *
 * Definition:
 * - NFC normalization is applied only to the counting copy.
 * - Each Han, Hiragana, Katakana, or Hangul letter is one word. A Chinese
 *   paragraph therefore has one word per ideograph, never one word total.
 * - A maximal run of other Unicode letters/numbers/marks is one word.
 * - U+0027 and U+2019 join a run only when both sides are non-CJK word code points.
 * - Combining marks never start a word.
 * - Punctuation, symbols, emoji, and whitespace are not words. Hyphens split,
 *   decimal points split, and URLs split at punctuation.
 */
export function countWords(input: string): number {
	const text = input.normalize("NFC");
	let count = 0;
	let inRun = false;
	let previousWasStandalone = false;

	for (let index = 0; index < text.length; ) {
		const codePoint = String.fromCodePoint(text.codePointAt(index) ?? 0);
		const width = codePoint.length;
		if (isJoinableApostrophe(text, index, inRun)) {
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isStandaloneWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			count++;
			inRun = false;
			previousWasStandalone = true;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (MARK_CODE_POINT.test(codePoint)) {
			// Marks belong to the preceding code point and never create a token.
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		if (isWordCodePoint(codePoint)) {
			if (!inRun && !previousWasStandalone) count++;
			inRun = true;
			previousWasStandalone = false;
			index += width;
			continue;
		}
		inRun = false;
		previousWasStandalone = false;
		index += width;
	}

	return count;
}

export interface WordLimitResult {
	readonly ok: boolean;
	readonly words: number;
	readonly maxWords: number;
	readonly remaining: number;
}

/** Evaluate a word cap without mutating the supplied text. */
export function evaluateWordLimit(input: string, maxWords: number): WordLimitResult {
	if (!Number.isInteger(maxWords) || maxWords < 0) {
		throw new RsiError("INTERNAL", "maxWords must be a non-negative integer.");
	}
	const words = countWords(input);
	return {
		ok: words <= maxWords,
		words,
		maxWords,
		remaining: Math.max(0, maxWords - words),
	};
}

/** Throw when text exceeds a word cap. The caller must not write on this error. */
export function assertWordLimit(
	input: string,
	maxWords: number,
	code: "MEMORY_WORD_LIMIT" | "DOCUMENT_WORD_LIMIT",
	label: string,
): number {
	const result = evaluateWordLimit(input, maxWords);
	if (!result.ok) {
		throw new RsiError(code, `${label} exceeds ${maxWords} words (found ${result.words}).`, {
			details: { words: result.words, maxWords },
		});
	}
	return result.words;
}

import { RsiError } from "./errors.ts";

export const DEFAULT_TIME_ZONE = "UTC";
export const CLOCK_FORMAT_PATTERN = /^\d{4}\/\d{2}\/\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$/;

export interface Clock {
	now(): Date;
}

/** Wall-clock source for the Supervisor and for tests injected into the Worker. */
export class SystemClock implements Clock {
	now(): Date {
		return new Date();
	}
}

/** Validate an IANA time zone or "UTC"; throws CONFIG_INVALID otherwise. */
export function assertValidTimeZone(timeZone: string): string {
	if (timeZone.trim().length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", "timeZone must not be empty.");
	}
	try {
		new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone }).format(0);
	} catch (error) {
		throw new RsiError("CONFIG_INVALID", `Invalid IANA time zone: ${timeZone}`, { cause: error });
	}
	return timeZone;
}

export interface ZonedParts {
	readonly year: number;
	readonly month: number;
	readonly day: number;
	readonly hour: number;
	readonly minute: number;
	readonly second: number;
}

export interface WallClock extends ZonedParts {}

function formatterFor(timeZone: string): Intl.DateTimeFormat {
	return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
		timeZone,
		calendar: "gregory",
		numberingSystem: "latn",
		hourCycle: "h23",
		year: "numeric",
		month: "2-digit",
		day: "2-digit",
		hour: "2-digit",
		minute: "2-digit",
		second: "2-digit",
	});
}

/** Read civil time fields in a specific zone. */
export function getZonedParts(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): ZonedParts {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const date = typeof instant === "number" ? new Date(instant) : instant;
	if (Number.isNaN(date.getTime())) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid Date value.");
	}
	const parts = formatterFor(timeZone).formatToParts(date);
	const values = new Map(parts.map((part) => [part.type, part.value]));
	const read = (name: Intl.DateTimeFormatPartTypes): number => {
		const value = values.get(name);
		if (value === undefined) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", `Missing ${name} in time zone formatting.`);
		return Number(value);
	};
	return {
		year: read("year"),
		month: read("month"),
		day: read("day"),
		hour: read("hour") % 24,
		minute: read("minute"),
		second: read("second"),
	};
}

export function isLeapYear(year: number): boolean {
	return year % 4 === 0 && (year % 100 !== 0 || year % 400 === 0);
}

export function daysInMonth(year: number, month: number): number {
	switch (month) {
		case 2:
			return isLeapYear(year) ? 29 : 28;
		case 4:
		case 6:
		case 9:
		case 11:
			return 30;
		default:
			return 31;
	}
}

function assertCivilDate(parts: WallClock): void {
	if (
		!Number.isInteger(parts.year) ||
		parts.year < 1 ||
		parts.year > 9999 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.month) ||
		parts.month < 1 ||
		parts.month > 12 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.day) ||
		parts.day < 1 ||
		parts.day > daysInMonth(parts.year, parts.month) ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.hour) ||
		parts.hour < 0 ||
		parts.hour > 23 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.minute) ||
		parts.minute < 0 ||
		parts.minute > 59 ||
		!Number.isInteger(parts.second) ||
		parts.second < 0 ||
		parts.second > 59
	) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid civil date/time.");
	}
}

function utcMsFromCivil(parts: WallClock): number {
	const date = new Date(0);
	date.setUTCFullYear(parts.year, parts.month - 1, parts.day);
	date.setUTCHours(parts.hour, parts.minute, parts.second, 0);
	return date.getTime();
}

function nextDay(parts: WallClock): WallClock {
	const date = new Date(utcMsFromCivil({ ...parts, hour: 0, minute: 0, second: 0 }));
	date.setUTCDate(date.getUTCDate() + 1);
	return {
		year: date.getUTCFullYear(),
		month: date.getUTCMonth() + 1,
		day: date.getUTCDate(),
		hour: 0,
		minute: 0,
		second: 0,
	};
}

/**
 * Parse the exact wall-clock syntax YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss.
 *
 * 24:00:00 is accepted only when minute and second are both zero, and is
 * normalized to 00:00:00 on the next civil day. 24:00:01 is invalid.
 */
export function parseWallClock(input: string): WallClock {
	const match = /^(\d{4})\/(\d{2})\/(\d{2}) (\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(input);
	if (!match) {
		throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Expected YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss.");
	}
	const [, yearText, monthText, dayText, hourText, minuteText, secondText] = match;
	const parts: WallClock = {
		year: Number(yearText),
		month: Number(monthText),
		day: Number(dayText),
		hour: Number(hourText),
		minute: Number(minuteText),
		second: Number(secondText),
	};
	if (parts.hour === 24) {
		if (parts.minute !== 0 || parts.second !== 0) {
			throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "24:00:00 is the only valid hour-24 spelling.");
		}
		const rolled = nextDay({ ...parts, hour: 0 });
		assertCivilDate(rolled);
		return rolled;
	}
	assertCivilDate(parts);
	return parts;
}

/** Format parsed civil fields as the canonical second-resolution timestamp. */
export function formatWallClock(parts: WallClock): string {
	assertCivilDate(parts);
	const pad = (value: number, width: number): string => String(value).padStart(width, "0");
	return `${pad(parts.year, 4)}/${pad(parts.month, 2)}/${pad(parts.day, 2)} ${pad(parts.hour, 2)}:${pad(parts.minute, 2)}:${pad(parts.second, 2)}`;
}

/** Normalize a wall-clock string, including the only legal 24:00:00 spelling. */
export function normalizeWallClock(input: string): string {
	return formatWallClock(parseWallClock(input));
}

/** Offset of a zone at an instant, in milliseconds east of UTC. */
export function getTimeZoneOffsetMs(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): number {
	const epochMs = typeof instant === "number" ? instant : instant.getTime();
	if (!Number.isFinite(epochMs)) throw new RsiError("TIME_INVALID", "Invalid instant.");
	const wholeSecond = Math.trunc(epochMs / 1_000) * 1_000;
	const parts = getZonedParts(wholeSecond, timeZone);
	return utcMsFromCivil(parts) - wholeSecond;
}

export interface ParsedZonedDateTime {
	readonly timeZone: string;
	readonly epochMs: number;
	readonly normalized: string;
	readonly ambiguous: boolean;
}

/**
 * Resolve a wall-clock string in a zone.
 *
 * A skipped local time (spring-forward gap) is an error. An ambiguous local
 * time (fall-back overlap) resolves to the earlier instant and reports
 * `ambiguous: true`; this policy is deterministic across hosts.
 */
export function parseZonedDateTime(input: string, timeZone: string): ParsedZonedDateTime {
	assertValidTimeZone(timeZone);
	const wallClock = parseWallClock(input);

	for (let deltaHours = -36; deltaHours <= 36; deltaHours++) {
		offsetCandidates.add(getTimeZoneOffsetMs(targetMs + deltaHours * oneHour, timeZone));
	}

	for (const offset of offsetCandidates) {
		const candidate = targetMs - offset;
		const candidateParts = getZonedParts(candidate, timeZone);
		if (
			candidateParts.year === wallClock.year &&
			candidateParts.month === wallClock.month &&
			candidateParts.day === wallClock.day &&
			candidateParts.hour === wallClock.hour &&
			candidateParts.minute === wallClock.minute &&
			candidateParts.second === wallClock.second

		timeZone,
		epochMs: matches[0] ?? targetMs,
		normalized: formatWallClock(wallClock),
		ambiguous: matches.length > 1,
	};
}

export function currentTimeSuffix(instant: Date | number, timeZone: string): string {
	return `(Current Time: ${formatTimestamp(instant, timeZone)})`;
}

import { parseWallClock, parseZonedDateTime } from "./time.ts";

export const SLEEP_TOOL_NAME = "sleep";
export const MIN_SLEEP_DURATION = "1s";
export const SLEEP_DURATION_PATTERN = /^([1-9]\d{0,14})([smh])$/;

export type SleepDurationUnit = "s" | "m" | "h";

export interface SleepDuration {
	readonly raw: string;
	readonly amount: number;
	readonly unit: SleepDurationUnit;

export type SleepRequest =

	| { readonly kind: "absolute"; readonly until: string; readonly normalizedUntil: string };

export interface SleepRequestInput {
	readonly duration?: unknown;
	readonly until?: unknown;
}

const UNIT_MS: Readonly<Record<SleepDurationUnit, number>> = {
	s: 1_000,
	m: 60_000,
	h: 3_600_000,
};

/** Parse one relative duration in s, m, or h. Fractions, zero, and signs are rejected. */
export function parseSleepDuration(input: string): SleepDuration {
	const match = SLEEP_DURATION_PATTERN.exec(input);
	if (!match) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "duration must be a positive integer followed by s, m, or h (for example 30m).");

	const unit = match[2] as SleepDurationUnit;
	if (!Number.isSafeInteger(amount) || !Number.isSafeInteger(amount * UNIT_MS[unit])) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "duration is too large to represent safely.");
	}
	return { raw: input, amount, unit };
}

/**
 * Validate the sleep tool's mutually exclusive forms.
 *
 * Exactly one of `duration` and `until` must be present. Supplying both,
 * neither, null, or an empty string is an error.
 */
export function parseSleepRequest(input: unknown): SleepRequest {
	if (typeof input !== "object" || input === null || Array.isArray(input)) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "sleep requires an object with exactly one of duration or until.");
	}
	const record = input as Record<string, unknown>;
	const hasDuration = record.duration !== undefined;
	const hasUntil = record.until !== undefined;
	if (hasDuration && hasUntil) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_BOTH_FORMS", "sleep accepts exactly one of duration or until, not both.");
	}
	if (!hasDuration && !hasUntil) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "sleep requires exactly one of duration or until.");
	}
	if (hasDuration) {
		if (typeof record.duration !== "string" || record.duration.length === 0) {
			throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "duration must be a non-empty string.");
		}
		return { kind: "relative", duration: parseSleepDuration(record.duration) };
	}
	if (typeof record.until !== "string" || record.until.length === 0) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "until must be a non-empty string.");
	}

	const canonical = `${String(wallClock.year).padStart(4, "0")}/${String(wallClock.month).padStart(2, "0")}/${String(wallClock.day).padStart(2, "0")} ${String(wallClock.hour).padStart(2, "0")}:${String(wallClock.minute).padStart(2, "0")}:${String(wallClock.second).padStart(2, "0")}`;
	return { kind: "absolute", until: record.until, normalizedUntil: canonical };
}

export interface SleepDeadline {
	readonly request: SleepRequest;
	readonly timeZone: string;
	readonly requestedAtMs: number;
	readonly deadlineMs: number;
	readonly deadlineLocal: string;
	readonly ambiguity?: "earlier";
}

/** Compute the absolute deadline in UTC milliseconds. Past absolute deadlines are rejected. */
export function computeSleepDeadline(input: unknown, now: Date, timeZone: string): SleepDeadline {
	const request = parseSleepRequest(input);
	const requestedAtMs = now.getTime();
	if (!Number.isFinite(requestedAtMs)) {
		throw new RsiError("SLEEP_INVALID", "now must be a valid instant.");
	}
	if (request.kind === "relative") {
		const durationMs = request.duration.amount * UNIT_MS[request.duration.unit];
		const deadlineMs = requestedAtMs + durationMs;
		if (!Number.isSafeInteger(deadlineMs)) {

		timeZone,
		requestedAtMs,
		deadlineMs: parsed.epochMs,
		deadlineLocal: parsed.normalized,
		...(parsed.ambiguous ? { ambiguity: "earlier" as const } : {}),

	return state.status === "active" && now.getTime() >= state.deadlineMs;

nodes.task:
为当前仓库实现 RSI-Agent 的公共基础和跨模块契约。现有仓库只有完整的 Pi 源码目录 pi/，其中 packages/coding-agent 的包名是 @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent，版本 1.4.0。不要修改 pi/ 的任何文件，不提交 Git commit。最终产品是在 Pi 原生 Runtime 之外新增可在 Linux Docker 中 24H 运行的外层 Runtime；不是重写 Agent，也不是只写设计稿。

用户约束：使用 Pi 原生 read/write/edit/bash，并实际安装、加载 npm:pi-continuity 和 npm:pi-better-web-search；可自行编写和加载扩展工具。Linux bubblewrap 保护 Pi、RSI/Runtime 源码及人工系统提示词只读，其余容器/VM 的普通磁盘和网络尽量不受限制。不能让 Agent 使用 /quit、/model、/thinking 或等价控制入口；/reload 必须先在隔离子进程中静态语法检查及 3 秒 Mock 加载，失败作为工具错误返回，成功运行 3 个健康对话轮次再生成 LKG 快照，重载崩溃/卡死由外部 Watchdog 回滚。人工不可变系统提示词 + Agent 可修改的 Memory.md 两部分；Memory 最大 500 词，超额报错且旧内容完全不变，每次成功修改返回 [System Meta: Current Memory Usage: N / 500 words]；同一个 tool loop 下一次模型请求也要把最新 Memory 放在 system 位置而不是历史消息。所有工具结果最终包含 (Current Time: YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss)。管理的 Markdown 放 markdowns/，每篇 <=1000 词、总数 <=20，index.md 使用 md名/description/链接位置三列；索引与实际文件不一致，每次工具结果尾部警告；read(index.md) 动态追加各文件词数、mtime、过去24小时 read 次数，不能写回文件。sleep 工具恰好提供互斥的相对 duration（s/m/h）和绝对 until（YYYY/MM/DD HH:mm:ss）参数；只有显式 sleep 能让自主循环暂停。MCP 和 Skill 各最多5个，沿用 Pi 原生策略，不添加立场提示词。用户明确禁止我们撰写、改写任何 Agent 提示词；只接受人工提供的系统提示词文件，Memory 初始化可为空，运行事件/配额元数据不是人格提示词。

先读 Pi 的 SDK、extensions、packages、mcp、skills 文档与实际导出类型，验证选型。特别注意 context_with_system 是每次请求的边界，before_agent_start 只按 run 不足以保证 Memory 实时性；agent_settled 而非 agent_end 才是最终空闲；SDK 要 bindExtensions 才能正确启动插件。不得把同名 GitHub 项目的 pi-continuity 当成指定 npm 包，必须检查实际 npm manifest。

你的独占实现范围：rsi/package.json、rsi/package-lock.json、rsi/tsconfig.json、rsi/.gitignore、rsi/src/shared/**、rsi/scripts/check* 和测试运行器（如需要），以及 markdowns/architecture.md、初始 markdowns/index.md。新增独立 TypeScript ESM 包，Node >=22.19，严格类型，使用可擦除 TS；固定直接依赖精确版本及 lock，不依赖修改/构建 vendored Pi。优先使用与仓库一致的已发布 Pi SDK，核实可安装性。依赖安装用 --ignore-scripts，不运行 Pi 的 build/全套测试；不要自动执行第三方 lifecycle scripts。定义可实际复用的 config 校验、路径布局、统一 Unicode 词数算法、时钟/时间格式、错误及有 request id 的受限 IPC 协议与端口接口。脚本提供独立包 typecheck 和无真实模型调用的测试入口；其他模块将据此并行实现，不要写它们的占位实现。

在公共契约中明确：可信外部 Supervisor 与 bubblewrap 中的 Pi SDK Worker 分进程；插件绝不在 Supervisor 中加载。定义知识存储/工具前后处理、SandboxLauncher、预检/快照/Watchdog、Pi Worker、自主 Loop、sleep、命令控制的依赖注入接口和事件。IPC 要覆盖按请求取得最新 Memory、托管文档事务、read 统计/工具结果装饰、预检后的 reload、sleep 门控、健康 turn 和心跳，避免后续模块互相猜 API。Worker 的 IPC 独立于可被插件 console.log 污染的 stdout，限制消息尺寸并处理错误/背压。最终主入口由后续集成完成。

安全设计优先采用：托管知识目录在 Worker/b​​ash 中只读，由外部文档 broker 为原生 write/edit 的托管路径完成校验后原子提交；这样 bash/扩展直接 fs 写不能绕过 Memory 的不保存约束。除受保护的知识/代码/控制状态外不要建立额外网络/磁盘白名单。明确保护目录的所有可见别名、独立 /proc、能力剥离，隐藏外部状态、快照与控制实现。不要把工具事件 hook 当成 OS 沙箱。说明代理持久化知识文档的管辖范围：只读 Pi/vendor 文档不计入20篇，原生 Skill 的 SKILL.md 是单独资源而不是把所有 node_modules README 算入配额；对 Agent 管理的知识文档不得以换目录、软/硬链接绕过。若全容器任意 .md 创建与广泛磁盘权限存在无法同时强制的边界，必须在设计中准确说明实际保证，不能以事后文件 watcher 冒充原子拒绝。Memory.md 和 index.md 默认放在运行数据的 markdowns/，两者计入20篇；建议索引有自身条目以满足所有 md 均被列出的文字要求。人工系统提示词用外部 .txt 路径，缺少则 fail closed，不生成示例提示词。

确定统一的时间语义（默认 UTC，可配置 TZ，日志注明）、按秒格式，以及 24:00:00 只在分秒都0时规范化成次日00:00:00。词数不能把整段中文当1词；给英文、中文、混合文本可复现的定义及边界测试。睡眠状态与已验证插件 generation/LKG 必须在 Agent 不可写的外部状态中持久化。明确健康3轮计数和候选目录在预检/加载/晋升期间不可变，避免 TOCTOU。

architecture.md 是开发/运维文档不是提示词，控制在1000词以内；所有新增 Markdown 均在根 markdowns/。跑你创建的测试及独立包 check，把准确的接口、各模块目录约定、运行命令和已验证依赖写入继承文件。必要时在 rsi/reports/foundation.txt 记录尚待真实 Linux 验证的事项，不宣称完成未实现功能。不要修改其他模块将拥有的实现目录。
